title: Josh and Chuck's Christmas Extravaganza
summary: Christmas holiday special of Stuff You Should Know. Josh and Chuck cover a grab-bag of Christmas topics: the origins of caroling and the word "carol," wassail, figgy pudding, the poinsettia and its Mexican origins with Joel Roberts, the 1914 Christmas Truce in World War One trenches, the origins of Christmas stockings and Saint Nicholas, white Christmases and NOAA's odds map, and a closing reading of "'Twas the Night Before Christmas." Includes a few sponsor reads and a Christmas-music banter intro.

segments.title: Holiday special intro and Christmas music banter
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck introduce the Christmas holiday special and chat about favorite Christmas songs and albums, including Bing Crosby, Vince Guaraldi, and the Waitresses.

segments.title: Origins of Christmas caroling
segments.summary: The word carol is traced to dance, with roots in Latin and Greek. Caroling is linked to Northern European Yule festivities, wassail, and churchgoers going door to door. Carols became religious when Saint Francis of Assisi made upbeat Nativity carols in the thirteenth century. The feudal singing-for-supper idea and a probably-untrue legend of a missing girl named Carol Poles are also mentioned.

segments.title: Christmas carol trivia and figgy pudding
segments.summary: Discussion of the Twelve Days of Christmas dating to eighteenth-century England, the German origin of O Tannenbaum whose tune is used for several state anthems, and what figgy pudding is.

segments.title: Poinsettia origins and myths
segments.summary: The poinsettia is native to southern Mexico and was brought to the US by diplomat Joel Roberts in 1828. Its Mexican name and legend are covered, along with its toxicity myths: it is only mildly toxic to people and somewhat toxic to cats. National Poinsettia Day is December twelfth.

segments.title: Transition to Christmas Truce story
segments.summary: Brief banter introducing the next story, which Chuck connects to the film Joyeux Noel.

segments.title: The 1914 Christmas Truce
segments.summary: During World War One, Pope Benedict XV called for a Christmas truce, which was largely rejected. On Christmas Eve 1914 in Flanders, Belgium, German and British soldiers decorated trenches with trees, sang carols, exchanged gifts, and met in no man's land, where a soccer match was played. Fighting resumed afterward; the origin of the term no man's land is also discussed.

segments.title: Origins of Christmas stockings
segments.summary: Hosts share childhood stocking memories, then trace the stocking tradition to Saint Nicholas and the story of gold coins dropped down chimneys, along with the Dutch wooden shoe custom of leaving hay for Sinterklaas's horse and the early nineteenth-century American adoption.

segments.title: White Christmas: songs, odds, and freak snowstorms
segments.summary: Irving Berlin's White Christmas and its recordings are discussed. NOAA's map of white Christmas chances is described, with Atlanta under five percent and Calumet, Michigan over ninety percent. London betting odds and fluke white Christmases in New Orleans in 2004 and Australia in 2006 are mentioned.

segments.title: Introduction to the story reading
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck set up the reading of 'Twas the Night Before Christmas, crediting Clement C. Moore with writing it for his children.

segments.title: Reading: 'Twas the Night Before Christmas
segments.summary: Chuck and Josh read Clement C. Moore's poem 'Twas the Night Before Christmas, also known as A Visit from Saint Nicholas, in full.

segments.title: Closing sponsor read and credits
segments.summary: Closing sponsor read and website and app promotion.
